annotation.title_clean: Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 May 2006 on machinery, and amending Directive 95/16/EC (recast)
annotation.title_en: Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 May 2006 on machinery, and amending Directive 95/16/EC (recast)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 157
annotation.summary_en: The EU Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC (recast) harmonises essential health and safety requirements for machinery placed on the EU market. It sets risk assessment, CE marking, conformity assessment, notified bodies, harmonised standards and market surveillance. It is the core safety framework for industrial robots, and it has since been replaced by the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230.
key_provisions_or_claims: Manufacturers must carry out risk assessment and meet Annex I essential health and safety requirements before placing machinery on the market
CE marking, EC declaration of conformity and technical file are required
Conformity assessment procedures are tiered, with stricter ones for Annex IV higher-risk machinery, including notified bodies
Compliance with harmonised standards gives a presumption of conformity
Member States must set up market surveillance and penalties, and apply the rules from 29 December 2009
